# Z-order implementation for character Alfred (2026-01-26 13:20Z)

_**User (2026-01-26 13:31Z)**_

ok in room 5 sprites 0 and 1 have zOrder of 80 respectively. We settled that alfred had a zorder of 10, so the result is right now alfred walks in front of those sprites, whilst in the original game it walks behind them. I suspect it has to do with the scale factor even though i dont really see the character scalking in this room.

I want you to check the current implementation against the one on the ghidra decompilation and determine whats a correct z order for Alfred, and whether it depends on scale / y position.

Do not use heredoc python. Rename functions and vars as you go.

## Summary of Changes

I analyzed the Ghidra decompilation and the existing documentation, and found that:

### The Problem
The original code used a **hardcoded z-order of 10** for Alfred:
```cpp
if (_room->_currentRoomAnims[i].zOrder > 10) { /* behind Alfred */ }
if (_room->_currentRoomAnims[i].zOrder <= 10) { /* in front of Alfred */ }
```

This meant Alfred was always at z-order 10, regardless of his Y position. Sprites with z=80 (like in room 5) would always appear BEHIND Alfred since 80 > 10.

### The Original Game's Formula (Verified in Ghidra @ 0x15a20-0x15a3d)
Alfred's z-order is **dynamically computed** from his Y position:
```c
alfred_z_order = ((399 - alfred_y_position) & 0xFFFE) / 2 + 10
```

This creates depth perspective:
- **Y=399 (bottom/near)**: Alfred z = 10 (frontmost)
- **Y=200 (middle)**: Alfred z = 109
- **Y=0 (top/far)**: Alfred z = 209 (backmost)

### The Fix
I added a helper function and updated `updateAnimations()`:
```cpp
static int calculateAlfredZOrder(int alfredY) {
    return ((399 - alfredY) & 0xFFFE) / 2 + 10;
}
```

Now sprites with z=80 will:
- Appear **IN FRONT** of Alfred when Alfred is near the bottom (Y > ~240, giving Alfred z < 80)
- Appear **BEHIND** Alfred when Alfred is near the top (Y < ~240, giving Alfred z > 80)

This matches how the original DOS game handles z-ordering, creating proper depth-based sprite layering.
